title: Patterns intermediate representation
description: owasp_rules.json: the OWASP Core Rule Set as owasp2json.py reads it, and what every converter builds on. Documented in docs/ir.md. Any change to this file bumps schema_version, and tests/test_ir_schema.py fails if it does not.

schema_version.description: The version of this schema the document was written for.

_provenance.description: Where the rules come from. The document is a derived work of the CRS (Apache-2.0); see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

source_ref.description: The one upstream tag the rules were read from.

score_defaults.description: What each anomaly level is worth, as REQUEST-901-INITIALIZATION.conf sets it. Defaults: a deployment can override them in crs-setup.conf.

data_files.description: The phrase lists that `@pmFromFile` rules read, by file name, as the CRS ships them in rules/*.data: the phrases of each, in file order, without comments or blank lines. Only the files a rule names are here, and each file a rule names is.

rule.description: One directive of the CRS, in file order. A chain is several of these: see chain.

id.description: The CRS rule id, or "no_id" for a record that has none: a link of a chain, or a SecRuleUpdateTargetById.

pattern.description: Deprecated. The operator string as the converters read it, operator included ("@lt 1"), with doubled backslashes folded. Replaced by operator, removed when the converters move to it.

location.description: Deprecated. The variable list folded into one request component, "UNKNOWN" when none of them is mapped. Replaced by variables.

severity.description: crs_severity folded into high, medium or low; medium when the rule declares none. A choice of this project, not of CRS.

transformations.description: The t: chain the operator argument is written to run after, in order, without t:none.

action.description: The disruptive action the rule declares. null means it inherits SecDefaultAction's, which is the case for every link of a chain.

directive.description: SecRule is a rule. SecRuleUpdateTargetById adds a target to an existing rule (target_rule_id) and is not one itself.

phase.description: The phase the rule runs in, 1 to 5. A link of a chain has its head's. null only for a directive that is not a rule.

variables.description: What the operator is matched against, in the order written. For SecRuleUpdateTargetById, the targets it adds or excludes.

operator.description: null for a directive that is not a rule.

crs_severity.description: The severity as the rule writes it, such as CRITICAL. null when it declares none.

score.description: The anomaly score the rule adds when it matches. For a chain, on its head, and added only when every link matches. null when the rule adds none.

chain.description: null for a rule that is not part of a chain.

target_rule_id.description: The rule a SecRuleUpdateTargetById changes. null for a SecRule.

category.description: The part of the CRS the rule comes from: the name of its file without the number and the extension (SQLI, XSS, RCE, ...).

name.description: The variable or collection, as written (ARGS, REQUEST_HEADERS, TX, ...).

selector.description: What follows the first colon, as written. Wrapped in slashes it is a regular expression, except for XML, where it is XPath. null when the whole collection is meant.

count.description: True for &VAR: the number of matching variables, not their values.

excluded.description: True for !VAR: taken out of the list, not added to it.

name.description: The operator without the @, as written (rx, pm, pmFromFile, detectSQLi, lt, ...). rx when the rule names none.

negated.description: True for !@op: the rule matches when the operator does not.

argument.description: What follows the operator name, exactly as written: nothing is unescaped, and macros such as %{tx.x} are not expanded. Empty for an operator that takes none.

level.description: What the rule adds is this level's points in score_defaults.

chain.description: A chain is a head and the links after it, in file order, and matches when every one of them does. Only the head carries an id, a phase, an action, a severity and a score.

head.description: The id of the head of the chain this record is part of.

position.description: 0 for the head, then 1, 2, ... for each link.
